title: Ch-V-R
hook: chaver, chavruta: friend, study partner, joining

segments.voice: Yesterday, Y-Sh-V: yashav, to sit, to dwell, to settle. Your line was sit and learn. What did you sit with, and did you stay? Today, the person sitting across from you. Day one thousand four hundred eighteen.

The sound reaches you first: a big room full of voices, and nobody quiet. People sit in pairs over open books, reading a line out loud, pointing, arguing, asking each other what it means and then asking again. Nobody is lecturing. Somebody laughs; somebody slaps the table. In a traditional study hall, this is what learning can sound like. Each pair is a chavruta. Each partner is a chaver. Today's root is the one that ties them together.
screen: `A ROOM FULL OF VOICES.` → `PAIRS OVER OPEN BOOKS.` → `CHAVRUTA.`

segments.voice: Ch-V-R. Chet, vet, resh. To join, to connect. A chaver is a friend, a companion; a chavruta, a study partnership. Turn it a few ways. First, joining. When the tabernacle is built, its curtains are "coupled together one to another," and the Hebrew uses this root. A psalm calls Jerusalem "a city that is compact together," joined to itself, the same letters again. A friend, in this root, is someone you're fastened to. Second, choosing. The sayings of the fathers teach: make for yourself a teacher, and acquire for yourself a friend. A teacher you appoint. A friend, the Hebrew says, you acquire, as if it costs you something. Third, the hard story. The Talmud tells of Choni, who slept for seventy years. He wakes and goes to the study hall, and hears the scholars saying how clear the teaching used to be in Choni's day. He tells them who he is. They don't believe him, and don't give him the honor due. Heartbroken, he prays for mercy and dies. And the sage Rava says: this is why people say, o chavruta o mituta. Either companionship, or death. Fourth, the pair. That's the weight a study partner carries. Your chaver catches what you missed, pushes back, asks the question you were avoiding. In this root, a friend isn't a spectator to your life. A friend is joined to the work.
screen: `CURTAINS COUPLED TOGETHER.` · `ACQUIRE YOURSELF A FRIEND.` · `CHONI, UNRECOGNIZED.` · `EITHER COMPANIONSHIP, OR DEATH.` · then, large: `A FRIEND IS JOINED TO THE WORK.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: join a friend. Settle, and breathe. Bring one friend to mind: someone you'd call if something went wrong, or someone you've drifted from. See their face. Remember one thing you know because of them: a skill, a habit, a way of seeing. Hold it for a breath. Then think of one small way to join them: a call, a walk, a question about something they love, a page you could read together. Hold that plan gently. If you pray, you can pray for them by name. The bell holds the time.
screen: `ONE FRIEND.` · `ONE THING YOU KNOW BECAUSE OF THEM.` · `ONE WAY TO JOIN THEM.`

segments.voice: Ch-V-R. Chet, vet, resh: chaver, a friend, and chavruta, a study pair. To be joined. Today's word.
Your line: friendship joins. Today, ask one friend a real question about something they know well, and listen the way a study partner would. Day one thousand four hundred eighteen.

howItsDone: In a traditional beit midrash, students learn in chavruta, pairs who read the text aloud and question each other; Pirkei Avot teaches 'acquire for yourself a friend', and the Talmud's saying 'either companionship or death' comes from the story of Choni.

options: you start over with new friends.
heartbroken, you pray for mercy and die.
fork.reveal: the Talmud says he prayed and died, and Rava said: o chavruta o mituta, either companionship or death.

original.note: Aramaic: a study partnership, from chet, vet, resh, the root of chaver, friend.

trapdoor: what you thought: a chaver is just a buddy.
what it means: Ch-V-R is joining: curtains coupled together, a city compact together, a friend fastened to you.
what a scholar hears: Taanit 23a: Choni, unrecognized in the study hall, and Rava's o chavruta o mituta.

sources.quoted: a city that is compact together

notes: Exodus 26:3 chovrot; Psalm 122:3 shechubrah lah yachdav: both Ch-B-R (the index spells it Ch-V-R). Confirm.
Pirkei Avot 1:6 (Yehoshua ben Perachyah): aseh lecha rav, u-kneh lecha chaver. 'Acquire... as if it costs you something' is an interpretive gloss offered by many commentators; confirm wording.

Taanit 23a paraphrased: Choni sleeps seventy years, is not believed at the study hall, is not given honor, prays for mercy and dies; Rava: 'hence the saying, either companionship or death' (o chavruta o mituta). 'Seventy years' is in the Talmud's text. Confirm.
Hook describes a traditional study hall in pairs; 'can sound like' rather than a general claim. Confirm.
Original: chavruta is Aramaic; note says so.
Editor: practice no longer tells the listener to feel grateful. Choni story (Taanit 23a) and quotations checked; no other change.
